scope: Corollary 5.4 (A finite predictor list for scheduled opponents) of the manuscript “Pointwise convergence of triple ergodic averages for mixing transformations” (preprints/Pointwise-convergence-of-triple-ergodic-averages-for-mixing-transformations-October-4-2026/pointwise-triple-ergodic-averages-mixing-transformations.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 154 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e76fd7732f10b250), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 34. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The manuscript presents this as a result of other work, which it uses; the attribution names that work in the manuscript's own words. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix the two bounded scalar atoms φi, φj on J′, of complexity at most Hlow, and let B ≥ 1. There is a finite index set A, a bound Dpred, scalar coefficients cr,α, and fixed triples (ψa,α, ψb,α, λα) on J′ with ∥ψe,α∥∞ ≤ 1, such that #A, complexity(ψe,α), |cr,α| ≤ Dpred, log Dpred ≤ poly 1 + B + log(2Hlow)  . Here cr,α is a scalar depending only on the fixed pair, its scalar construction, B, and the dyadic scale r; it is zero unless |λα|r2 ≤ Dpred. The list and these coefficients are chosen before any opposing sequences or completed high catalogs. Define its forms explicitly by Tα I (za, zb) := |I|−2 Z R2 wI(x, t)e(λαt2 )ψa,α(ya)za(ya) · ψb,α(yb)zb(yb) dx dt. (5.15) For every dyadic K ⊆ J′, selected finite use collection U below K, and pair of admissible opposing sequences on K, define the actual error eI by the per-cell identity L φi,φj I (za,I, zb,I) = X α∈A c|I|,αTα I (za,I, zb,I) + eI. (5.16) Then, uniformly over those opposing sequences and their completed catalogs, X I∈U |I||eI| ≤ e−B poly log(2Dh), 1 + L  |K|. (5.17) The error eI may depend on the opposing sequence; the assertion is its aggregate bound.
